name: Radar sweep reveal

source.description: 2 inspected reference films (batch-4, batch-6, 2026-11-26): a SaaS launch sweeps a wedge over concentric rings and pops labelled signal points as it passes them.

technique: A wedge rotates over concentric rings and each labelled point appears as the wedge passes it, so discovery is shown as scanning: the viewer watches the system find things instead of a list appearing.
purpose: Show discovery as scanning: the viewer watches the system find things instead of a list appearing.
visual_behaviour: A wedge sweeps round concentric rings; each labelled point pops in as the wedge passes it.
mechanics: Wedge as a conic gradient or SVG path rotating 0 -> 360 deg linearly over 2-4 s; each point's reveal time = its angle / 360 x period; point pop (scale 0 -> 1, back.out) plus a label slide; rings static; optional pulse ring on each hit; point angles from a seeded PRNG.

decomposition.timing: One sweep in 2-4 s; points about 0.2-0.4 s apart (reference 12-17.6 s).

use_cases: Showing many signals found over time
failure_modes: Points that appear before the wedge reaches them
Too many labels to read at 720p

implementation.approach: Rotate an SVG wedge (or a conic gradient) 0-360 degrees linearly over 2-4 s; each point's reveal time = its angle / 360 x period; pop each point with Studio.space.pop (back.out) and slide its label; seed the point angles with the Studio PRNG, never Math.random. Not built as a component.

provenance.observed: On cream, a peach wedge sweeps over concentric rings and labelled signal points pop as it passes (12-17.6 s).
Linear variant: a red glowing horizontal line sweeps down a transcript panel and each timestamped row appears as the line passes (about 4.0-4.5 s, 10 fps).

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
